terms.meaning: The state legislature's houses, which with the Governor make the State Legislature.
The lower house, of the people's elected representatives (MLAs).
The upper house; no more than one-third the size of the Assembly.
The constitutional head of a state, nominated by the President for five years.
When the state government is dissolved, the Governor runs the state for the President.

items.name: How states are organised
items.formula: States were made on a linguistic basis; Kannada is Karnataka's language.
items.example: They follow the Central Government's model.

items.name: States with two houses
items.formula: Only six states have both an Assembly and a Council; Karnataka is one.
items.example: All others have only an Assembly.

items.name: Karnataka Legislative Assembly
items.formula: 224 elected seats; MLAs serve five years and elect a Speaker.
items.example: The nominated Anglo-Indian seat ended with the 104th Amendment in 2020.

items.name: Who can be an MLA
items.formula: A citizen of at least 25, holding no office of profit, not insolvent.
items.example: MLAs must solve their constituency's problems.

items.name: Powers of the Legislative Assembly
items.formula: Final say on money matters; can remove ministers by a no-confidence motion.
items.example: MLAs also vote in the President's election.

items.name: Karnataka Legislative Council
items.formula: 75 members, some nominated by the Governor, others elected by MLAs, local bodies, graduates and teachers.
items.example: MLCs must be 30 and serve six years.

items.name: Karnataka's government buildings
items.formula: Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru; Suvarna Soudha in Belagavi.
items.example: The High Court is in Bengaluru.

items.name: Who can be Governor
items.formula: A citizen of at least 35, not a member of Parliament or a state legislature.

items.name: Powers of the Governor
items.formula: Appoints the Chief Minister and ministers; bills need the Governor's assent.
items.example: In a crisis the Governor reports to the President.

items.name: Powers of the Chief Minister
items.formula: Head of the state government: advises on appointing ministers, allots portfolios, can dismiss ministers.
items.example: The CM keeps good Centre-State relations.

mistakes.text: The Governor is the constitutional head; the Chief Minister is the real chief executive.
The Governor is nominated by the President, not elected by the people.
Vidhana Sabha matches the Lok Sabha (lower house); Vidhana Parishat matches the Rajya Sabha (upper house).
